Aliases:
INS 260
E 260
E260
Ethanoic Acid
Glacial Acetic Acid

Category:
Acidity Regulator / Preservative

source.title: 21 CFR 184.1005 - Acetic acid; JECFA evaluations; EFSA opinion

text:
Function:
Controls pH, adjusts tartness and acidity, provides antimicrobial preservation by lowering water pH, and acts as a flavoring agent.

Description:
Acetic acid is a two-carbon organic acid (CH3COOH). In commercial food applications, it is produced either by microbiological fermentation of ethanol by acetobacter bacteria (as found in vinegar) or via industrial synthetic carbonylation of methanol followed by purification to food grade standards.

source.title: 21 CFR 184.1005 - Acetic acid; JECFA evaluations; EFSA opinion

text:
Regulatory Information:
Affirmed as Generally Recognized as Safe (GRAS) by the US FDA under 21 CFR 184.1005 for use as an antimicrobial, flavoring, and pH control agent. Evaluated by JECFA (JECFA No. 81) with an Acceptable Daily Intake (ADI) of "not limited" / "not specified". Authorized as an approved food additive in the European Union as E 260 under Regulation (EC) No 1333/2008 at quantum satis.

source.title: 21 CFR 184.1005 - Acetic acid; JECFA evaluations; EFSA opinion

text:
Assessment Notes:
Acetic acid is an intermediate in normal human metabolism (Krebs cycle). Non-toxic at dietary consumption levels; pure undiluted glacial acetic acid is corrosive, but food-grade dilutions are considered safe and biologically well-tolerated.

Cheese powder is produced by melting natural or processed cheese into a liquid slurry, often with the addition of water, emulsifying salts, and sometimes milk solids, and subsequently spray drying the mixture into a fine, free-flowing dry powder.

Function:
Controls pH, provides a tart acidic taste, enhances antioxidant activity, and acts as a preservative and chelating agent in foods and beverages.

Description:
Weak organic tricarboxylic acid found naturally in citrus fruits, commercially produced by microbial fermentation of carbohydrate substrates such as molasses using Aspergillus niger.

Citric acid is an essential physiological intermediate in the cellular citric acid (Krebs) cycle and is fully metabolized by the human body.

Serves as a primary grain base, structural starch component, texture former, and bulking ingredient in extruded snacks, baked goods, cereals, and batters.

Description:
Corn meal is a coarse flour ground from clean, sound dried maize kernels (Zea mays). It can be whole grain or degerminated, where the germ and outer bran are removed during dry milling to enhance shelf stability and starch content.

In India, regulated by FSSAI under Food Safety and Standards (Food Products Standards and Food Additives) Regulations, 2011, Regulation 2.4.24 covering Degermed Maize (Corn) Meal and Maize Grits.

Ribonucleotides are naturally occurring purine derivatives metabolized into uric acid in the human body. Individuals with clinical metabolic purine disorders such as hyperuricemia or gout typically manage dietary purine intake.

text:
Function:
Serves as a frying medium, cooking medium, lipid base, and textural component in processed foods and snacks, providing mouthfeel, crispness, and dietary energy.

Description:
Edible vegetable oil is a broad regulatory classification for food-grade refined, cold-pressed, or blended oils extracted from plant sources (such as oilseeds, legumes, grains, or fruit mesocarp). In food manufacturing and packaged snacks, the term denotes plant-derived lipids suitable for human consumption without designating a singular botanical species.

source.title: FSSAI Regulations 2.2; Codex CXS 210-1999; 21 CFR 101.4

text:
Regulatory Information:
In India, FSSAI regulates edible vegetable oils under Regulation 2.2 of the Food Safety and Standards (Food Products Standards and Food Additives) Regulations, 2011, establishing quality, purity, acid value, and labeling parameters for single and blended edible vegetable oils. Codex Alimentarius Commission establishes international quality parameters under CXS 210-1999 (Standard for Named Vegetable Oils) and CXS 19-1981 (Standard for Edible Fats and Oils). In the United States, FDA regulations under 21 CFR 101.4(b)(14) govern vegetable oil ingredient declarations.

source.title: FSSAI Regulations 2.2; Codex CXS 210-1999; 21 CFR 101.4

text:
Assessment Notes:
Generic edible vegetable oil declarations are nonspecific as to the exact plant origin unless qualified by specific parenthetical oil declarations on the product packaging. Edible vegetable oils are standard food macro-ingredients composed of fatty acid triglycerides with no established Acceptable Daily Intake (ADI) limit.

Ingredient:
Iodised Salt

Aliases:
Iodized Salt
Iodized Table Salt
lodized Salt
Salt
Table Salt
Common Salt
Edible Common Salt
Sodium Chloride

Category:
Seasoning / Fortified Salt

source.title: FSSAI Regulation 2.4.1 (Edible Common Salt / Iodised Salt); Codex CXS 150-1985; WHO Fortification Guideline

text:
Function:
Serves as an essential mineral seasoning, dietary sodium and chloride nutrient, flavour enhancer, and food preservation agent by controlling microbial growth and water activity; acts as a public health delivery vehicle for dietary iodine.

Description:
Iodised salt is food-grade crystalline sodium chloride (NaCl) fortified with trace quantities of iodine, typically in the form of potassium iodate (KIO3) or potassium iodide (KI). It is produced by solar evaporation of seawater or mining of rock salt deposits, followed by refining and spray-fortification with food-grade iodizing agents to ensure uniform distribution.

source.title: FSSAI Regulation 2.4.1 (Edible Common Salt / Iodised Salt); Codex CXS 150-1985; WHO Fortification Guideline

text:
Regulatory Information:
In India, regulated under FSSAI Food Safety and Standards (Food Products Standards and Food Additives) Regulations, 2011, Regulation 2.4.1 (Standards for Edible Common Salt / Iodised Salt), mandating that salt for direct human consumption must contain not less than 30 ppm of iodine on dry basis at the manufacturing level and not less than 15 ppm at retail. Internationally governed by Codex Alimentarius Standard for Food Grade Salt (CXS 150-1985) and affirmed as GRAS by US FDA under 21 CFR 182.1.

source.title: FSSAI Regulation 2.4.1 (Edible Common Salt / Iodised Salt); Codex CXS 150-1985; WHO Fortification Guideline

text:
Assessment Notes:
Safe and essential mineral staple. Universal salt iodisation is recognized by the World Health Organization (WHO) and UNICEF as the primary, most cost-effective public health strategy to eliminate iodine deficiency disorders (IDD), goiter, and preventable cognitive deficits. WHO guidelines recommend moderate overall sodium intake (less than 2g sodium / 5g salt per day) while maintaining universal salt iodisation.

text:

L-lactic acid is an endogenous intermediate in human cellular carbohydrate metabolism. In infant foods, JECFA and EFSA note that D-lactic acid should be limited because infant metabolism processes the D-isomer more slowly.

text:

US FDA classifies MSG as Generally Recognized as Safe (GRAS) under 21 CFR 182.1. JECFA allocated an Acceptable Daily Intake (ADI) of "not specified" in 1987. FSSAI approves its use under Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) in specified food categories per Food Safety and Standards Regulations.

text:

Extensive scientific evaluations by JECFA, FDA, and EFSA have found no causal relationship between MSG consumption at typical dietary levels and reported adverse symptoms in the general population.

Composed primarily of oleic acid (approx. 40-43%), palmitic acid (approx. 40-45%), and linoleic acid (approx. 10-12%). Liquid at ambient room temperature, it can cloud or form reversible crystals at cooler storage temperatures.

source.title: 21 CFR 184.1622 - Potassium chloride; JECFA evaluations; EFSA opinion

text:
Function:
Replaces sodium chloride to reduce sodium content while contributing salty flavor, and functions as a mineral nutrient, flavor enhancer, and firming agent.

Description:
Naturally occurring inorganic metal halide salt composed of potassium and chlorine, extracted from mineral deposits such as sylvite or carnallite and purified through crystallization.

source.title: 21 CFR 184.1622 - Potassium chloride; JECFA evaluations; EFSA opinion

text:
Regulatory Information:
US FDA affirms potassium chloride as Generally Recognized as Safe (GRAS) under 21 CFR 184.1622 and permits the alternate name "potassium salt" on ingredient statements. JECFA evaluated potassium chloride in 1979 and assigned an ADI of "not limited". EFSA re-evaluated potassium chloride (E 508) in 2019 and concluded that it raises no safety concern at reported food additive uses.

source.title: 21 CFR 184.1622 - Potassium chloride; JECFA evaluations; EFSA opinion

text:
Assessment Notes:
Provides bioavailable potassium, an essential dietary electrolyte. It imparts a salty taste profile that can carry bitter or metallic notes at higher sodium-substitution ratios.

Aliases:

E551
Silica
Amorphous Silica
Synthetic Amorphous Silica

Category:
Anticaking Agent

source.title: EFSA E 551 evaluation; 21 CFR 172.480; JECFA INS 551

text:
Function:
Prevents clumping and caking, promotes powder flowability, adsorbs excess moisture, and serves as a carrier for flavors and active components in dry food mixtures.

Description:
Silicon dioxide is a chemical compound of silicon and oxygen (SiO2). For food use, it exists exclusively in synthetic amorphous (non-crystalline) form, produced via wet processes (precipitated silica or silica gel) or vapor thermal processes (pyrogenic/fumed silica).

source.title: EFSA E 551 evaluation; 21 CFR 172.480; JECFA INS 551

text:
Regulatory Information:
Approved by the US FDA under 21 CFR 172.480 as a direct food additive for anticaking use at levels not exceeding 2 percent by weight of the food. Evaluated by JECFA (INS 551) with a group ADI of "not specified". Authorized in the European Union as food additive E 551 under Regulation (EC) No 1333/2008, with EFSA re-evaluations confirming no safety concern across authorized uses.

source.title: EFSA E 551 evaluation; 21 CFR 172.480; JECFA INS 551

text:
Assessment Notes:
Synthetic amorphous silica does not possess crystalline quartz toxicity; it is biologically inert, insoluble in gastrointestinal fluids, and largely excreted unabsorbed. No safety concern identified at permitted regulatory levels.

text:
Function:
Provides sweet taste, enhances flavor profiles, contributes bulk and mouthfeel, acts as a humectant to retain moisture, depresses freezing point, and assists in preservation by lowering water activity.

Sugar is a disaccharide carbohydrate composed of glucose and fructose subunits (C12H22O11). It is commercially extracted and refined by pressing juice from sugarcane (Saccharum officinarum) or sugar beets (Beta vulgaris), followed by clarification, evaporation, and crystallization.

Classified nutritionally as a macronutrient and a free/added sugar. source.title: 21 CFR 184.1979; FSSAI Dairy Regulations; Codex CXS 289-1995

text:
Function:
Provides dairy solids, enhances texture, binds water, improves browning, and serves as a carrier for flavorings and seasonings.

Description:
Whey powder is obtained by spray drying liquid whey, the fluid co-product resulting from the coagulation of milk by rennet or acid during cheese or casein manufacturing. It consists primarily of lactose, whey proteins (beta-lactoglobulin and alpha-lactalbumin), and mineral salts.

source.title: 21 CFR 184.1979; FSSAI Dairy Regulations; Codex CXS 289-1995

text:
Regulatory Information:
Affirmed as Generally Recognized as Safe (GRAS) by the US FDA under 21 CFR 184.1979. Regulated in India by FSSAI under Food Safety and Standards (Food Products Standards and Food Additives) Regulations, 2011, Regulation 2.1.18. Governed internationally under Codex Alimentarius Standard CXS 289-1995.

source.title: 21 CFR 184.1979; FSSAI Dairy Regulations; Codex CXS 289-1995

text:
Assessment Notes:
Contains milk protein and lactose; subject to mandatory declaration as a milk allergen in major regulatory jurisdictions. Consumed as a macronutrient food ingredient rather than an additive, with no numerical Acceptable Daily Intake (ADI) limit established under Good Manufacturing Practice.
